title: Add the fail-closed control_connection_read contract (always identity_unavailable until a sound handle-level proof exists)
outcome: TermAl can call control_connection_read on the original or resumed control child and get either control_connection_superseded or control_connection_identity_unavailable, never a possibly wrong path. Unknown recovery stays GAP until w-952b4211be2d proves the held file.
acceptance: A read-only control_connection_read on the same HostControlServer and SqliteStore, on a current serving connection (original or resumed), returns the actual opened SQLite main database's canonical database_path plus the fixed project_id and session_id only on a platform where the opened file can be proven to be the one at that path; no platform qualifies today. Until one does, and whenever that proof fails, it refuses with control_connection_identity_unavailable and never returns a possibly different file. It first verifies the current connection with the existing storage check, and reuses or extracts readiness's canonical path formatting.

It adds no token, grant, bind, schema change or new registry, and it is answered by the serving child itself. A separate readiness process or the child's config, home or marker never stands in for it.

Tests cover: on every platform the read refuses with control_connection_identity_unavailable on a current original or resumed connection and never returns a path; a superseded connection is refused with control_connection_superseded first; and the read changes no state and needs no grant.
The host protocol docs describe the read and its fail-closed use; existing fencing behavior (an old bind before resume is still allowed, never after) is unchanged.
